notes:
Account snapshot and POC notes:

- Background: Hawthorne runs global TMS + customer-facing tracking chat. Latency is a strict business KPI for chat and live shipment status (target perceived latency <= 120ms for short replies). Heavy reranking workload for carrier selection (batch), and periodic large-scale embedding reindex jobs for nightly sync.

- Why Redwood: They want predictable unit economics (reserved GPUs) + single API across hosted/dedicated/private. Interested in Redwood's dedicated capacity guarantees and Optimize suggestions to lower unit token costs.

- Requirements (from CTO & infra lead):
  * Chat latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms for 2k concurrent users, p50 <= 70ms. Streaming ok for longer responses.
  * Reranking throughput: sustain 6k small requests/min during peak (each request ~200 tokens), batch-friendly.
  * Embeddings: nightly bulk embed job for 15M documents (throughput >200k vectors/hr desirable).
  * Model preferences: prefer open/quantizable models; evaluate 16k vs 32k context variants.
  * Security: VPC-only, SAML SSO, KMS integration, audit logs retained 13 months; data residency for EU customers.

- POC scope (agreed):
  1) Baseline perf on 4x A100-80GB vs 2x H100-80GB (single model variant, fp16) using Redwood dedicated POC cluster.
  2) Model tuning matrix: context length (8k/16k/32k), quantization (fp16 / q4f16 / int8-gptq), batch sizes (1/4/8/16) and KV cache TTL settings (no-cache / per-session / sticky-prefix).
  3) Stress & failover: scale-to-failure test (burst 3x expected), validate automatic fallback to smaller model variant without SLA break.
  4) Cost/delta analysis: CPU/GPU-hours, tokens/sec, per-request cost estimates, reserved capacity amortization.

- Early POC observations (Elena Park notes, 2026-02-18 call ff_20260218_hawthorne_poc_call):
  * FP16 baseline on A100 stable, p95 chat ~180ms (above target).
  * q4f16 quant reduced latency by ~12-18% for tail requests; quality checks OK for simple tracking queries but showed regressions on multi-hop summarization.
  * Batching (4->8) improved throughput for reranking but increased p95 for chat; suggests separate routing policies per route.
  * KV cache helped multi-turn chat latency (p50 down to ~50ms) but had memory pressure on 4x A100 config when using 32k context.

- Reserved GPU planning considerations discussed with infra:
  * Two acceptable deployment plans: (A) 8x A100-80GB dedicated (cheaper upfront) vs (B) 4x H100-80GB (higher single-request perf, fewer nodes).
  * Ops prefers fewer H100 nodes if Redwood can guarantee p95 latency SLO via kernel selection + batching controls.
  * Want explicit SLO language: objective p95 <= 150ms for chat on pinned model under committed throughput; credit model for SLO breaches; define maintenance windows and blackout periods.

- SLA / commercial negotiation points (legal & procurement flagged):
  * Include latency SLOs with credit percentages tied to monthly invoice (not just uptime).
  * Clear definition of 'compatible fallback' and billing when fallback model used.
  * Data residency and breach notification terms.
  * Op-ex vs cap-ex cost modeling for reserved capacity (term 12 vs 36 months).

- Action items / next steps (short):
  * SE (Elena) to run targeted bench: q4f16 vs int8-gptq on both GPU SKUs for 16k/32k contexts by 2026-03-10 (in progress).
  * AE (Marcus) to share draft reserved capacity pricing spreadsheet and two commercial scenarios by 2026-03-08 (done, awaiting review).
  * Legal to receive SLA draft 2026-03-05; procurement to return comments by 2026-03-15.
  * Customer to provide 3 representative prompt sets for quality-replay; scheduling recording session.

- Quotes / customer language captured: "We need predictable tail latency — if a user hits chat during peak it must feel instantaneous. We'll accept small model quality downgrade only if it's invisible to users."

- Risks:
  * 32k context memory pushes need for more GPU RAM or aggressive KV eviction; may force H100 plan.
  * Quantization regression risk on complex summarization; needs eval corpus.
